from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Power Series Foundation", 
                          ["Consider an infinite sum of powers.", 
                           "As s increases, terms shrink rapidly.", 
                           "This allows the series to converge."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a circle representing a Taylor series convergence
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#3498DB", stroke_width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3498DB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show an animation of terms adding up to a function
        # Using a simple representation
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#E74C3C") for _ in range(5)])
        dots.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(dots, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#E74C3C")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the convergence concept
        square = Square(side_length=1.0, color="#2ECC71", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(square))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#2ECC71")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Riemann Zeta function sums integers.",
            "It extends into the complex plane.",
            "This is known as analytic continuation.",
            "The domain covers the whole plane.",
            "Values are filled in smoothly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Riemann Zeta Function", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        zeta_sum = MathTex(r"\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}", color="#F1C40F")
        convergence_text = MathTex(r"\text{Re}(s) > 1", color="#2ECC71")
        
        self.place_at_grid(zeta_sum, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(convergence_text, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Initial state (hidden)
        zeta_sum.set_opacity(0)
        convergence_text.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"), FadeIn(zeta_sum))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"), FadeIn(convergence_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#9B59B6"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = ["Zeta connects to prime numbers.", "A product formula reveals this.", "Primes act like fundamental building blocks.", "Each prime contributes a factor.", "They define the Zeta structure."]
        self.setup_layout("The Euler Product Formula", lines)
        
        # Animation Elements
        zeta_eq = MathTex(r"\zeta(s) = \prod_{p} (1 - p^{-s})^{-1}").scale(1.2)
        prime_group = VGroup(*[Text(str(p), color="#9B59B6") for p in [2, 3, 5, 7, 11]]).arrange(RIGHT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.play(FadeIn(prime_group))
        self.place_at_grid(prime_group, 'B3', 1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.place_at_grid(zeta_eq, 'D3', 1.0)
        self.play(Write(zeta_eq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        zeta_eq.set_color("#9B59B6")
        self.play(Indicate(zeta_eq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        bracket = Brace(zeta_eq, DOWN, color="#34495E")
        self.play(Create(bracket))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.play(FadeOut(bracket), FadeOut(prime_group))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Zeros hold the prime secret.",
            "They live in the strip.",
            "The critical line is key.",
            "All non-trivial zeros lie here.",
            "This defines prime number distribution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Riemann Hypothesis: The Critical Strip", lecture_lines)
        
        # Visualization objects
        # Critical strip: 0 < Re(s) < 1. In complex plane, let's represent as a rectangle.
        strip = Rectangle(height=6, width=1, color="#E67E22", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(strip, 'C3')
        
        # Critical line: Re(s) = 1/2.
        line = Line(start=UP*3, end=DOWN*3, color="#FFFFFF")
        line.move_to(strip.get_center())
        
        # Zeros
        zeros = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#D35400", radius=0.1) for _ in range(5)])
        for i, zero in enumerate(zeros):
            zero.move_to(line.get_center() + UP * (i*1.2 - 2.4))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#E67E22"))
        self.play(Create(strip))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#D35400"))
        self.play(FadeIn(zeros))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Why It Matters: Summary and Impact", [
            "Zeta explains prime pattern randomness.",
            "Its zeros predict distribution.",
            "Cryptography relies on this insight."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a glowing icon for prime distribution (using dots)
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#1ABC9C", radius=0.05) for _ in range(50)])
        for dot in dots:
            dot.move_to(np.array([np.random.uniform(2, 6), np.random.uniform(-2, 2), 0]))
        self.place_at_grid(dots, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(dots))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#1ABC9C"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show zeros predicting distribution (lattice structure)
        lattice = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#1ABC9C", radius=0.07) for _ in range(25)])
        lattice.arrange_in_grid(5, 5, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(lattice, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(dots, lattice))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#1ABC9C"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out to show impact (a padlock/symbol)
        lock = Text("🔒", font_size=48).set_color("#7F8C8D")
        self.place_at_grid(lock, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeOut(lattice), FadeIn(lock))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#7F8C8D"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Riemann Zeta Function: Bridging Primes and Patterns

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Power Series Foundation
sections.content: Establish the concept of infinite series convergence. Briefly explain how $f(s) = \sum 1/n^s$ behaves as 's' changes, focusing on the transition from a simple harmonic series to convergent patterns.
sections.example: Visualize a 'Zeta-bot' collecting energy blocks; if the blocks get small fast enough (s > 1), the bot's total energy stays finite.

sections.title: Defining the Riemann Zeta Function
sections.content: Introduce $\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}$. Explain the domain extension from real numbers to the complex plane (Analytic Continuation) using a visual map of the complex plane.
sections.example: An animation showing a ripple in a pond spreading from the real axis to the entire complex plane, 'filling in' the missing values.

sections.title: The Euler Product Formula: The Prime Connection
sections.content: Connect the summation formula to the product of primes: $\zeta(s) = \prod_{p} (1 - p^{-s})^{-1}$. This is the 'DNA' of the function, revealing that the Zeta function is fundamentally built from prime numbers.
sections.example: A mechanical sieve animation where prime numbers act as 'gates' that filter out non-prime integers, leaving only the prime structure behind.

sections.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: The Critical Strip
sections.content: Introduce the 'Critical Strip' (0 < Re(s) < 1). Explain that all 'non-trivial zeros' of the function appear to lie on the line Re(s) = 1/2. Visual representation of the function's value turning into zero at these specific points.
sections.example: An archer (representing a mathematician) aiming at a target where the 'bullseye' is the critical line; landing a shot on this line helps predict the distribution of primes.

sections.title: Why It Matters: Summary and Impact
sections.content: Conclude by linking the zeros of the Zeta function to the 'randomness' vs 'structure' of prime numbers. A brief mention of its application in modern cryptography.
sections.example: Show a chaotic swarm of prime numbers transforming into a perfectly aligned geometric lattice once the 'Zeta key' is applied.
